4a_initial_conditions.summary: Experiment protocol is sound but first ~3.5 min of cold-start transient is missing from all listeners

protocol.description: run_coldstart.sh prompts operator to power on all nodes, marks t=0, then capture_coldstart.py opens serial ports. Nodes cold-boot, enumerate USB, and begin transmitting. Listeners log LPD/LRD frames with device uptime (now_ms) as the time axis.

gap_between_poweron_and_first_data.description: All 6 listeners show a 3.0-3.6 min gap between power-on (now_ms=0) and first usable LPD/LRD frame. This gap includes nRF52 boot, DW1000 init, PLL lock, and USB serial enumeration. The initial (fastest) portion of the crystal warm-up transient is NOT captured.
gap_between_poweron_and_first_data.significance: The fastest thermal transient is the initial 0-3 min after power-on (crystal self-heating from ambient). This is exactly the window that is missing. The reported cfo_start values already reflect 3+ min of warm-up, so the true cold-start excursion is LARGER than what the analysis reports.

boards_cold_at_t0.description: run_coldstart.sh prerequisite line 21 states 'ALL UWB nodes have been powered off for 2+ hours'. No independent verification exists (no temperature measurement at t=0). However, the consistent 3+ min boot gap across all 6 listeners and the monotonic CFO drift from first sample are consistent with a genuine cold start.
boards_cold_at_t0.confidence: Plausible but unverified — no temperature data at t=0

source_locking.description: Both capture (live) and analysis (offline) lock onto a single dominant TX source (0xb15a in all listeners) to avoid mixing per-transmitter clock offsets. This is correct methodology.

4b_cfo_excursion_and_stability.summary: NO listener reaches CFO stability within 90 min. The analyze_coldstart.py report correctly states 'NOT REACHED' for all 6, but this refutes any prior '30-min pre-warm' claim. Even a 4x-relaxed drift threshold (0.20 ppm/min) is never sustained.

stability_criteria.note: Threshold derived from overnight steady-state drift rate

drift_rate_at_time_marks_ppm_per_min.description: Median drift rate in ±2.5 min window around each mark

30_min_prewarm_claim.explanation: At 30 min, drift rates range 0.08-0.18 ppm/min across listeners — 2-4x above the 0.05 ppm/min stability threshold. At 90 min, drift rates are STILL 0.10-0.18 ppm/min. The drift does NOT converge to zero within the 90-min capture; it appears to plateau at ~0.1-0.2 ppm/min, suggesting either (a) the crystal never reaches thermal equilibrium on a 90-min timescale, or (b) the residual drift is not thermal but noise/jitter in the CFO estimate itself.

ranging_error_implication.worst_case_excursion: L9336: 1.50 ppm → 0.225 m range bias change over 90 min
ranging_error_implication.note: This is the differential CFO (listener vs transmitter 0xb15a). In Alt-SS-TWR the relevant quantity is the tag-anchor pair CFO, which may be larger or smaller depending on both devices' warm-up states.

4c_cfo_to_temperature_relationship.summary: No independent temperature measurement exists. CFO is used as a temperature proxy but the proxy is unvalidated: no TC_SARL reads, no nRF52 TEMP reads, no IR camera images saved, and cross-listener correlation is negligible (median Spearman rho = +0.17), proving per-board dynamics dominate over shared ambient temperature.

ss_twr_init_c_1210.guard: None — unconditionally compiled. Raw temp/vbat codes are emitted as a ;T trailer on the TR line per the comment at ss_twr_init.c:1202-1204.

DW1000_TC_SARL.evidence: The tag-side call (ss_twr_init.c:1210) is unconditionally compiled and reads DW1000 temp every 30s. However, the ;T trailer rides the tag->master-tag->host text passthrough — it is NOT part of the over-the-air UWB frame that listeners receive. Listeners see only LPD/LRD fields (rcph, rxtofs, ttcki, agc) from the blink/response packets. The anchor-side call (ss_twr_resp.c:1014) embeds temp in the V3 response payload but is compiled out by default. Therefore NO temperature data appears in the listener raw logs used by this cold-start experiment.
DW1000_TC_SARL.reason_not_used_in_experiment: capture_coldstart.py:14 states 'the on-chip TC_SARL sensor is NOT read — doing so wedges the SPI clock domain'. The tag firmware does read it (unconditionally), but the value does not propagate to the listener serial output that the cold-start capture records.

nRF52_TEMP_peripheral.evidence: apps/tag/build-tag-fast/zephyr/.config:1057 CONFIG_HAS_HW_NRF_TEMP=y, but no sd_temp_get() or NRF_TEMP access in application code

IR_camera.evidence: run_coldstart.sh:27 mentions IR camera as prerequisite; run_coldstart.sh:10 'Spatial thermal imaging is done separately with the IR camera (manual)'; NO .jpg/.tiff/.csv files in run directory

independent_temperature_measurement.conclusion: ZERO independent temperature data points exist in this dataset

crystal_type.evidence: deca_device.c:242-257 reads OTP XTAL trim and applies via dwt_setxtaltrim(); FS_XTALT register defined in deca_regs.h:1037
crystal_type.implication: CFO-to-temperature mapping is nonlinear and position-dependent on the parabola; without knowing each board's turnover temperature and operating point, CFO cannot be converted to °C

cross_listener_consistency.test: Spearman rank correlation of binned CFO curves (5s bins) across all 15 listener pairs
cross_listener_consistency.interpretation: If CFO drift were driven by shared ambient temperature, all same-room listeners would show rho > 0.8. Median rho = 0.17 proves each board's CFO is dominated by board-specific thermal dynamics (crystal self-heating, PCB thermal mass, mounting, individual XTAL characteristics), NOT shared environmental temperature.
cross_listener_consistency.implication: CFO stability of one board does NOT predict CFO stability of another, even in the same environment. A pre-warm time derived from one board is not transferable.

proxy_validity_assessment.verdict: CFO is a QUALITATIVE indicator of thermal activity, NOT a calibrated temperature measurement
reasons: No independent temperature ground truth to validate against
XTAL frequency-temperature curve is parabolic, not linear — same ΔT gives different ΔCFO depending on operating point
Near the crystal turnover temperature, CFO is insensitive to temperature changes (flat top of parabola)
Cross-listener rho = 0.17 means per-board factors dominate — 'temperature proxy' overstates what CFO actually measures

The experiment title says 'thermal characterization' but what it actually characterizes is CFO warm-up dynamics, which is a coupled function of crystal temperature, PCB temperature, ambient temperature, and possibly voltage regulation warm-up

overall_verdict.classification: ⚠️ QUALIFIED — experiment correctly executed within its design, but conclusions are weaker than stated
key_issues: 1. First ~3.5 min of cold-start transient missing (boot gap) — true excursion is larger than reported
2. NO listener reaches stability in 90 min by ANY reasonable threshold — '30-min pre-warm' claim is REFUTED
3. No independent temperature data — experiment measures CFO warm-up, not temperature warm-up
4. Cross-listener rho = 0.17 proves per-board dynamics dominate — pre-warm time is not transferable across boards
5. Residual drift at 90 min (0.10-0.18 ppm/min) may include measurement noise floor, not only thermal drift — the experiment cannot distinguish the two
what_the_experiment_DOES_establish: CFO excursion from first-sample to 90 min: 0.3-1.5 ppm across 6 listeners (lower bound; true cold-start value is larger)
CFO drift is still ongoing at 90 min at 0.10-0.18 ppm/min
At 0.50 ppm/min threshold (10x nominal), all listeners stable by 28 min — so the FAST transient is over by ~30 min, even if the SLOW tail is not
The analysis pipeline (capture + parse + bin + drift-rate + Spearman) is methodologically sound
The report correctly says 'NOT REACHED' and 'UNDETERMINED' — it does not overclaim
overall_verdict.recommendation: The analysis code is honest (correctly reports non-convergence). The gap is in the experiment design: add DW1000 TC_SARL reads (or at minimum nRF52 TEMP peripheral reads) to the firmware so CFO can be cross-validated against an independent temperature measurement. Save IR camera images with timestamps. Extend capture to 3-4 hours to find true convergence time, or determine that the residual drift is measurement noise.
